questions.q: In this lab's scenario, how does an Incident record link back to the Problem that caused it?
options: Through its problem_id field, which stores the Problem's sys_id
Incidents and Problems have no direct field-level relationship
Through a shared sys_id between the two records
Through the UI Action's Condition field directly
questions.explain: Every Incident caused by a given Problem stores that Problem's sys_id in its own problem_id field — that's what the UI Action's query filters on.

questions.q:
Look at this UI Action Condition field from the lab:

current.state == 6 && gs.hasRole('itil')

Why is this the right condition for the "Close All Related Tasks" button?
options: It only checks the user's role; the state check is unnecessary here
It closes the related incidents directly, without needing a Script field
It runs client-side, so it has no effect on whether the button appears
It hides the button from users without the itil role and until the Problem is actually Resolved
questions.explain: The Condition field is server-side and must return true for the button to render at all — gating on both role and state keeps it hidden until it's actually appropriate to show.

questions.q:
In the lab's server-side UI Action script, what does this line do?

inc.addQuery('problem_id', current.sys_id);
options: Filters the Incident query to only records linked to this specific Problem record
Sets the Problem's own problem_id field to its sys_id
Runs before current is available, so it would error
Filters on the Incident's active field instead of its problem_id
questions.explain: current.sys_id is the Problem record's own sys_id; the query uses it to find only the Incidents whose problem_id points back to this exact Problem.

questions.q: Why does the lab's UI Policy script call g_form.getUniqueValue() and run its own GlideRecord query inside onCondition_true, instead of reusing data already on the form?
options: It needs a live count of related, still-open Incidents at the exact moment the condition fires, which getUniqueValue() plus a fresh query can provide
GlideRecord cannot be called from any client-side script under any circumstances
The UI Action already stored this count somewhere g_form can read it directly
getUniqueValue() is required syntax for every UI Policy script, regardless of purpose
questions.explain: GlideRecord is callable from client-side scripts because the platform proxies it to the server — used here to get a current count rather than relying on a field that could be stale.

questions.q: Why does closing the related Incidents belong in the UI Action's script rather than the UI Policy's onCondition_true function?
options: A UI Policy's script is a client-side, continuously-evaluated mechanism meant for form feedback, not a one-time, server-side, record-mutating action triggered by a deliberate click
There is no real difference — either location would work identically
onCondition_true cannot call any GlideRecord methods at all
UI Actions cannot access current, only g_form
questions.explain: The UI Action is the deliberate, one-time, server-side action that should mutate records; the UI Policy's script is for live, client-side warnings as the form's condition changes.
